rules.instruction: When the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the participant’s described action as a distinct task; do not use the action itself as the start event.
rules.situation: the description states that a participant identifies or recognizes a need as an action that initiates the process, before describing subsequent work

rules.instruction: When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.
rules.situation: the description distinguishes activities or states a process outcome

rules.instruction: When the description says an activity may or may not occur before a later required activity: model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway, and merge the branches before the later required activity
rules.situation: the description says an activity may occur before a later required activity

rules.instruction: When the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives: Model each activity as a separate task on its own branch rather than combining the alternatives into one task; choose a gateway that matches whether one or multiple alternatives may be performed.
rules.situation: the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives

rules.instruction: When the description says an additional activity may be performed before a later activity that follows regardless: Model the additional activity as a distinct optional path that rejoins the main flow before the later shared activity.
rules.situation: the description says an additional activity may be performed before a later activity that follows regardless
